required_concepts: shape can have more than one line of symmetry
acceptable_paraphrases: no other shape with two lines of symmetry exists
a square is not the only shape with two lines of symmetry
other shapes such as a rhombus can have exactly two lines of symmetry
a parallelogram does not necessarily need to be a rectangle for it to have two lines of symmetry
critical_errors: saying all shapes with two lines of symmetry must be rectangles
incorrectly stating that only squares have two lines of symmetry
misconceptions: only squares can have two lines of symmetry
all shapes with two lines of symmetry must be rectangles
grading_notes: Credit should be given for correctly identifying that a shape does not have to be a rectangle and providing examples or explanations involving other shapes like rhombus or parallelogram. Deduct points for incorrect statements about the necessity of being a rectangle.
